results.title: No hallucinated or fabricated content
results.reason: The score is 1.00 because the actual output faithfully reproduces and expands upon the base blueprint, preserving all core elements—the IBM Confidential header, Target Outcome metrics (65-80% touchless, 40-55% FTE reduction, 3-day cycle time), APQC PCF 9.5 reference, the 14 atomic steps, business ontology, autonomy zone map (9 Green/4 Amber/1 Red), HITL specs, data products, integrations, MCP tools, agent definitions, context payloads, memory architecture, audit traces, orchestration, guardrails, and error handling. While it adds detail (Phases 4-6, extra columns) and generalizes appropriately for a client engagement, it introduces no contradictions with the contexts.

results.title: Customization stays consistent across phases and with the provided context
results.reason: The output is a substantial reformatting/renumbering of the base blueprint, migrating step IDs from 1.x notation to ATS1–ATS14, tool names to TOL1–TOL6, agents to AGN1–AGN7, and data products to DPS1–DPS6. Against evaluation criteria, propagation is largely strong and consistent: the ATS/AGN/TOL/DPS references align across the Atomic Step Register, Autonomy Zone Map, HITL spec, Data Products, Integration, Tool Register, Agent Register, and Phases 2–5. New autonomy-zone detail (ATS9 elevated to Green, ATS6 permanently Red) is coherent with the earlier register and HITL zones, and the added A2A contracts, guardrails, evals, and activation waves respect HITL and register definitions. However, there are notable flaws that count against full alignment: (1) the requested change ('Customization for the user's client, no additional details provided yet') is essentially null/undefined, so it is unclear what edit was actually requested and being propagated — the output appears to be a large unsupported expansion rather than a targeted change; (2) unsupported additions appear — e.g., Phase 6 introduces newly named agents ('Invoice Intake & Validation Agent', 'PO Matching Agent', 'Approval Routing Agent', 'Payment Scheduling Agent', 'Expense Reimbursement Agent') that do not map cleanly to the AGN1–AGN7 register, creating a mismatch/inconsistency in entity references; (3) minor propagation gaps such as Concur listed under DPS6 (Expense Policy Rules) plus 'Expense Reports and Receipts' where expense reports aren't a defined data product. Phase heading remains 'Phase 1: Cognitive Deconstruction' consistent with base. Overall the structural propagation and register consistency are good, but the ambiguous/absent target change plus the Phase 6 agent-naming divergence introduce unsupported additions and mismatched references that prevent a top score.

results.title: Domain plausibility and soundness (ungrounded, LLM knowledge)
results.reason: The blueprint is highly coherent and domain-realistic for accounts payable and expense reimbursement. Process steps (three-way match, GL coding, fraud detection, payment execution), roles (AP Specialist, Controller, Internal Audit, Treasury), and autonomy/HITL choices are logical — e.g., placing fraud detection in RED with dual approval, vendor bank-detail changes in AMBER for fraud risk, and advisory payment optimization in GREEN. Compliance references are appropriate and non-fabricated: SOX segregation-of-duties gates before GL posting, OFAC/EU sanctions screening before payment, APQC PCF 9.5, and 7-year financial records retention are all standard AP practice. Metrics and targets are largely reasonable: 22%→75% STP rate, cycle-time reductions, 40% cost-per-invoice reduction, and net-30 default terms all reflect plausible AP benchmarks. Fail-closed behavior on sanctions API outage and idempotency guards on postings reflect sound engineering practice. Minor tensions exist but none are implausible: the 'Screen Sanctions List' tool is oddly mapped to the fraud-detection skill rather than a distinct sanctions skill; the 65-80% touchless target header versus the 75% outcome-measurement target is slightly inconsistent; and the '100% detection rate on known typologies' fraud eval and 'zero missed fraud detections' Wave 1 exit criteria are aspirational for real fraud detection though defensible when scoped to known/synthetic cases. Model names and per-invoice cost figures are client-specific and not penalized under the ungrounded check. Overall the artifact is internally consistent, standards-appropriate, and free of claims that contradict accepted AP/finance practice.
